query: Optimizer behaviour change leading to errors
reference_answer:
The error itself seems to be a valid one. This error prevents the same module to be loaded more than once so that a single module has a single reference.

We can add a flag to opt-out that check, which means you may have multiple instances of a same module, as a temporary workaround. The real fix would be to solve https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/19323.

Retrying the import doesn't work here because that would not affect the code that is already executed.

query: Bundling a Vite app is creating unexpected circular dependencies
reference_answer:
@kevinfarrugia can you explain why circular dependencies isn't desired here? In practice, Rollup is able to analyze if a chunk was already loaded before and reuse some imports from it downstream, resulting in the circular dependencies, but they don't really affect the runtime. 

But as you may notice this happens with `manualChunks` as some code are placed in a less optimal place, resulting in Rollup doing optimizations to reuse imports from upstream chunks. (But it's not a big issue in practice as explained above)

query: Vite errors on import of @googlemaps/js-api-loader
reference_answer:
The error happens with named imports because in SSR, the package is externalized and Node uses the `main` field that is a UMD file. Only default import can be used for UMD files.
The error happens with default imports because in non-SSR, the package is not externalized and `module` field is used and that is a ESM file. Default import doesn't exist in that ESM file.

There's three ways I can think of to use this dependency:

1. Set `ssr.noExternal: ['@googlemaps/js-api-loader']` in `vite.config.ts`
2. Write a separate file for server and client
3. Patch `@googlemaps/js-api-loader`

[vite-plugin-cjs-interop](https://github.com/cyco130/vite-plugin-cjs-interop) might work as well.

query: 在使用antdesign-vue1.7.8的date-picker组件,通过moment库设置日期组件的default-value，使用webpack编译运行没有问题,改为vite编译运行后会报错
reference_answer:
`moment.isMoment` is bundled as undefined because `jsnext:main` points to `./dist/moment.js` which only have the default export. But `antdesign-vue` seems to expect the named export `isMoment` to exist, which is the case when the bundler did not respect `jsnext:main` field.

So, to summarize, this is caused by the expectation difference on the package side. Closing as there's not much we can do on Vite side.

query: 当构建库时使用 rollupOptions.output.banner 会导致打包出错误的 umd
Better handling of dynamic imports in dead code
Scripts set in manualChunks are loaded directly in front page, instead to be lazy loaded when needed
reference_answer:
**Summary:** Rollup 4.52.0 introduced `output.onlyExplicitManualChunks: true` option which you can use to solve this problem. This option can be used in Vite 5.x, 6.x, 7.x. In Vite 8, Vite will use Rolldown and it has the similar behavior to `output.onlyExplicitManualChunks: true` by default.

---

### Why this happens?

First, the app in the OP has a module graph like this:
```mermaid
graph LR
  index .-> ViteBugPage
  index --> react
  ViteBugPage --> react
  ViteBugPage --> fabric
  react --> commonjshelper
  fabric --> commonjshelper
```

and uses
```js
output: {
  manualChunks: {
    fabric: ['fabric'],
  },
},
```
.
When using `output.manualChunks` in the object form, ["each property represents a chunk that contains the listed modules and all their dependencies"](https://rollupjs.org/configuration-options/#output-manualchunks:~:text=each%20property%20represents%20a%20chunk%20that%20contains%20the%20listed%20modules%20and%20all%20their%20dependencies). `commonjshelper` is a dependency of `fabric`, so this means the output chunks will be
```mermaid
graph LR
  index["index + react"] .-> ViteBugPage
  ViteBugPage --> index
  ViteBugPage --> fabric
  index --> fabric
  fabric["fabric + commonjshelper"]
```
. As you can see in the graph, `index` imports `fabric + commonjshelper`.

### Fixing by tweaking your options
The problem is that `commonjshelper` is not in a separate chunk. If you use
```js
output: {
  manualChunks: {
    commonjshelper: ['\0commonjsHelpers.js'],
    fabric: ['fabric'],
  },
},
```
the output chunks will be:
```mermaid
graph LR
  index["index + react"] .-> ViteBugPage
  ViteBugPage --> index
  ViteBugPage --> fabric
  index --> commonjshelper
  fabric --> commonjshelper
```
You can achieve the same behavior with the function form as well:
```js
output: {
  manualChunks(id) {
    if (id === '\0commonjsHelpers.js') {
      return 'commonjshelper'
    }
    if (id.includes('/node_modules/fabric/')) {
      return 'fabric'
    }
  },
}
```
But the problem is that it's difficult to figure out the cause. `\0commonjsHelpers.js` module is a dependency of `fabric` because that's how the commonjs plugin works, but that's not something the user has to understand.

### Using `output.onlyExplicitManualChunks: true`

To solve that issue, Rollup 4.52.0 introduced `output.onlyExplicitManualChunks: true` option.

> By default, the function form will also merge dependencies of the returned ids into the manualChunk. If you need stricter behavior, you can use [output.onlyExplicitManualChunks](https://rollupjs.org/configuration-options/#output-onlyexplicitmanualchunks), which will be the default in Rollup 5.
> - From [Rollup documentation](https://rollupjs.org/configuration-options/#output-manualchunks:~:text=By%20default%2C%20the%20function%20form%20will%20also%20merge%20dependencies%20of%20the%20returned%20ids%20into%20the%20manualChunk.%20If%20you%20need%20stricter%20behavior%2C%20you%20can%20use%20output.onlyExplicitManualChunks%2C%20which%20will%20be%20the%20default%20in%20Rollup%205.)

By using this option you can have the option as:
```js
output: {
  manualChunks(id) {
    if (id.includes('/node_modules/fabric/')) {
      return 'fabric'
    }
  },
  onlyExplicitManualChunks: true,
},
```

But in this case, it seems Rollup disables the `manualChunks` option because the configuration causes a circular import:

> Circular chunk: ViteBug -> fabric -> ViteBug. Consider disabling the "output.onlyExplicitManualChunks" option, as enabling it causes the static dependencies of the manual chunk "fabric" to be bundled into the chunk "ViteBug".

The generated output was:
```mermaid
graph LR
  index["index + react + commonjshelper"] .-> ViteBugPage["ViteBugPage + fabric"]
  ViteBugPage --> index
```

It seems the warning goes away if I set the following option:
```js
output: {
  manualChunks(id) {
    if (id.includes('__vite-browser-external')) {
      return 'browser-external'
    }
    if (id.includes('/node_modules/fabric/')) {
      return 'fabric'
    }
  },
  onlyExplicitManualChunks: true,
},
```
The generated output was:
```mermaid
graph LR
  index["index + react + commonjshelper"] .-> ViteBugPage
  ViteBugPage --> index
  ViteBugPage --> fabric
  ViteBugPage --> browserexternal
  fabric --> browserexternal
  browserexternal --> index
```

### Using Vite 8 (Rolldown)
Rolldown does not support object form `manualChunks` option.

If you use function form `manualChunks` or the `codeSplitting` option which is the successor:
```js
output: {
  manualChunks(id) {
    if (id === '\0commonjsHelpers.js') {
      return 'commonjshelper'
    }
    if (id.includes('/node_modules/fabric/')) {
      return 'fabric'
    }
  },
  strictExecutionOrder: true,
}
```
```js
output: {
  codeSplitting: {
    groups: [
      {
        name: 'fabric',
        test: /\/node_modules\/fabric\//
      }
    ]
  },
  strictExecutionOrder: true,
}
```
The generated output was:
```mermaid
graph LR
  index["index + react"] .-> ViteBugPage
  index --> rolldownruntime
  fabric --> rolldownruntime
  ViteBugPage --> rolldownruntime
  ViteBugPage --> index
  ViteBugPage --> fabric
```
This is because Rolldown has a behavior similar to `output.onlyExplicitManualChunks: true`.

The `output.strictExecutionOrder: true` is needed because the configuration creates a circular import.

Side note: you need to set `legacy.inconsistentCjsInterop: true` for the project in the OP due to https://main.vite.dev/guide/migration#consistent-commonjs-interop.

Closing as this is fixed in Vite 8 beta. I think we still need to improve the things around the execution order problem, but we would love to hear your feedback after you try it!

reference_answer:
Also, just set it as an env variable and you don't have to call Vite's js script directly:

```sh
# where xxxx = (your memory in GiB) * 1024 - 512
export NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=xxxx'
```
